    "rationale": "Evidence: all 60 baseline trials (oval, s-bend, slalom, several seeds) went off track with max_error about 0.061 m, one line-loss event each, and progress of only 0.04 to 0.12. The robot is leaving the line early and never recovers, on every track. The cause is most likely the sensor span. Sensors sit at x = +/-0.02 m, and with a 12 mm footprint and a 25 mm tape (half-width 12.5 mm), the outer sensors see tape only while the line centre is within about 0.04 m of the axle. Beyond that the sum of readings drops below 0.05, the line is lost, and the robot drifts to the 0.06 m off-track limit. Changes: (1) Geometry: widen the sensor span to x = +/-0.03 m, with five sensors at 0.03, 0.015, 0, -0.015, -0.03 and weights unchanged at [1.0, 0.5, 0, -0.5, -1.0]. This gives line detection out to about 0.042 m offset for the outer sensors, and the centre sensors still read the line cleanly when centred. Sensor spacing of 15 mm stays well under the 25 mm tape width, so the signal stays continuous. (2) Controller: kd raised from 0.05 to 0.1 for more damping against the wider, faster steering. kp stays at 3.0 because the wider span already lowers the signal slope from about 150/m to about 100/m per metre of offset, which softens the effective gain. base_speed (1.6), ki (0) and line_loss (last_direction) are unchanged, so this revision changes one group (sensor span) plus a small damping adjustment. Expected result: line_loss_events drops to 0 or near 0, progress rises well above 0.12 on at least the oval, and max_error stays below the 0.06 limit. Hypotheses for the next revision: if steering_oscillation is high, lower kp to about 2.0; if rms_error is high with low oscillation, raise kp to 3.5 to 4.0; if completion is 0 with progress below 0.9 and completion_time is near 3 s, raise base_speed to about 1.9. Measurements wanted: which track fails first, the progress at failure, line_loss_events, and the max_error trend.",
